correctness.rationale: The Kraus operators satisfy completeness coordinatewise. The first branch has probability \(1/3\) and equal normalized Schmidt probabilities \(1/d\); the second has probability \(2/3\) and Schmidt rank one. Therefore the expected raw top concurrence is exactly \(1/(3d^d)\), versus input \((2d+1)/(3d)^d\). Their ratio is \(3^{d-1}/(2d+1)>1\), with the inequality proved from the base case \(d=3\) by induction. The finite checker independently replays representative dimensions in exact rational arithmetic; it is not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result identifies a structural boundary in a published concurrence hierarchy: the strongest raw member fails the operational average-LOCC condition in every dimension \(d\ge3\), with an explicit exact filter and an unbounded multiplicative violation. It also explains why the later \(d\)-th-root modification is mathematically substantive rather than a normalization convention.
